deep_dive.title: Disentangled Fine-Grained Prototype Learning for Incomplete Image-Tabular Classification
deep_dive.abstract: The missing-modality problem poses a significant challenge in image-tabular multimodal learning across a wide range of multimedia applications, including product understanding, recommendation systems, and medical diagnosis. This challenge is particularly pronounced when the two modalities are highly heterogeneous, as images and tabular attributes differ substantially in their semantic granularity and data distributions. Existing methods learn modality-invariant representations through disentanglement and alignment over global token-averaged features, capturing only coarse cross-modal consistency and overlooking fine-grained semantic and distributional misalignment, which hampers the exploitation of complementary cues under missing modalities. To address this, we propose DFPL, a novel framework for fine-grained prototype learning. Specifically, Shared-Specific Prototype Modeling (SSPM) extracts compact and diverse shared and modality-specific prototypes, and further performs prototype-level disentanglement to suppress redundant intra-modality correlations. Additionally, we propose a Prototype-guided Fine-grained Alignment (PFA) module that jointly enforces prototype-level distribution matching and prototype-to-class semantic alignment within a unified prototype space, thereby preserving both fine-grained distributional and semantic consistency across modalities. We further introduce a Class-aware Multi-scale Aggregation (CMA) module to adaptively aggregate shared semantics and modality-specific characteristics from global and prototype levels for robust predictions. Extensive experiments on three diverse image-tabular benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our method compared to the previous approaches under various missing-modality settings. Code will be made publicly available.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Proposes disentangled fine-grained prototype learning to handle missing modalities in image-tabular classification by addressing fine-grained semantic misalignment.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 本文针对图像-表格多模态分类中的缺失模态问题，指出现有解耦方法仅关注全局一致性，忽略了细粒度语义和分布错配。提出解耦细粒度原型学习，通过捕捉细粒度跨模态一致性来增强缺失模态下的互补信息利用。实验在多个数据集上验证了方法有效性，显著提升了缺失模态场景的分类性能。该工作直接涉及缺失模态和解耦表示，与用户需求高度吻合，但任务为分类而非情感识别。

quick_skim.title: To Be Multimodal or Not to Be: Query-Adaptive Audio-Visual Person Retrieval via Active Modality Detection
quick_skim.abstract: When retrieving a person from a video archive by voice and face, should the system be multimodal or not? In real-world broadcast archives, unlike curated benchmarks, a target may be heard but unseen, seen but unheard, or both. Fusing scores from an absent modality injects noise, degrading precision below the best unimodal system. We propose a query-adaptive framework that detects active modalities via cross-modal score consistency: when both modalities are active, files retrieved by one also score highly on the other; this agreement breaks down when a modality is absent. Classifiers driven by these cross-modal features achieve 89% detection accuracy. On the BBC Rewind corpus (with over 12,000 broadcast videos) the adaptive system attains 94.2% P@1, outperforming speaker-only (82.9%), face-only (93.4%), and fixed fusion (90.0%), recovering 64% of the gap to an oracle with ground-truth modality labels (96.6%).
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: Active modality detection handles missing modalities in audio-visual retrieval

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 在实际广播档案中，目标可能限于单模态，融合缺失模态降低精度。本文提出主动模态检测方法，通过跨模态得分一致性判断模态是否活跃，分类器准确率达89%。在BBC Rewind语料库上，自适应方法优于固定融合。该方法虽用于检索，但检测缺失模态的思路可迁移至情感识别。
